design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST. Graham Whitfield asks only to submit, himself, the release of the depreciation held back on his house now that the rebuild is finished (Public Adjuster Coordinated file). The release figure is the dwelling holdback (withheld depreciation less releases and write-offs) less an incurred-cost shortfall (the expected approvals, that is the approvals as recorded plus the scope_omission and price_variance supplements awaiting the carrier's decision, against the billed cost of the closed contract and the closed water job net of its credits), less the deductible carry, the advance recoupment, the code holdback cut and the supplement depreciation already paid. Its rule carries three action-form prerequisite sentences (each resolver may legitimately write nothing: a write-off of nothing or above the desk cap, a supplement below the minimum): it is not computed before the credited-line write-off is worked out and posted, fixed only after the category reassessment supplement is prepared and recorded, and waits until the regulated-scope supplement is prepared and recorded; the reassessment itself is fixed only after the regulated-scope supplement, whose pending request turns its regulated-cleanup family from the HEPA difference to the containment and HEPA difference. Skipping the write-off, the reassessment or the regulated-scope supplement each gives a different release; reading only the computation documents gives the whole-baseline figure. Difficulty comes from reading three charters' records (claims, water, rebuild) and four rules; each problem has exactly one tool.
SCOPE. Task 0 claims claims_ext_credited_line_writeoff, claims_ext_regulated_scope_supplement, claims_ext_category_reassessment_supplement and claims_ext_insured_depreciation_release with their four tools; task 1 holds the mold pair. Disjoint, complete.
DRAW. draw_counts.py task 0: prerequisite_problems 3, factor_counts [6,6,6,6]; every policy of the tree carries 6 factors.
PROBLEM TREE. Root claims_ext_insured_depreciation_release (owner=user: on this tier the company does not request depreciation). Edges: release <- credited_line_writeoff (gate rl_written), release <- category_reassessment_supplement (gate rl_pend_price), release <- regulated_scope_supplement (gate rl_pend_scope); reassessment <- regulated_scope_supplement (gate sc_reg_pending); all value_input, action form with fallback reasons. Seed: no write-off, no scope_omission or price_variance supplement; the only supplement (code_upgrade, number 1) names the contract and is decided. Order: the regulated-scope supplement before the reassessment (numbers 2 and 3 follow), the write-off anywhere before the release, the release last.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD. claims_evt_supplement: su_state approved; su_window approved 2026-05-28, last day 2026-11-24; su_pending max 2 (0 then 1 pending); minimum 250.00. claims_evt_writeoff: wo_state approved; desk cap 500.00; line room 36225.00. claims_evt_depreciation_release: dr_state approved; dr_complete contract closed; dr_window earliest ACV 2026-06-04, last day 2026-12-01.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. File SLI-HO-26-045276 (one water job, one contract, both linked; public adjuster Sutherland Public Adjusting). Write-off object: the initial dwelling approval (36225.00, withheld 6120.00). Supplements name the water job. Release names the closed contract.
WORLD ROWS. Water job (dispatched Gray Water Standard Loss on business hours, crew on site in 74 minutes, recorded category_3, class 2, 860 sq ft, single-family built 1974): extraction, pad removal and carpet detach-and-reset, containment, flood cut and baseboard, lead-safe setup and asbestos sampling (sampled 2026-05-04 before the 2026-05-05 flood cut), PPE 5 technician-days, technician and supervisor labor, the tear-out antimicrobial line (1660 sq ft at the 0.47 wet-wipe rate, dated the latest flood cut), the tear-out debris haul-off line (4 loads at the 267.50 sanitation rate, dated the latest flood cut) and the final HEPA vacuuming line (4020 sq ft at 0.31, dated the drying complete date), all priced under the published water rules, 5 days of air movers and LGR dehumidifiers within the 5-day cap, 4 monitoring visits (set day waived), moisture mapping and thermal imaging each billed twice; credits billing_error 14.40 (30 sq ft of pad removal), duplicate_line 145.00 and 95.00 (the repeated moisture mapping and thermal imaging), goodwill 75.00 (within the 150.00 cap), all within the 60-day window after the 2026-05-14 invoice; paid by the insured's check, closed. Contract (Standard Rebuild, signed 2026-05-26): contract sum 31850.00, building and electrical permit fees at cost with one expediting line per permit type, plan drawing and lead-safe setup, deductive carpet-install credit 160.60 (2026-08-05; the contract part at the carpet-install rate less the field-remeasure deduction, construction having started) followed by an owner-upgrade flooring change order 151.20 (2026-08-07), four draws at 10/30/30/remainder plus the fee payment, closed 2026-10-08. Claims (carrier payments issued to the insured only): advance 2000.00, initial approval 36225.00 on an estimate of 46982.40 (5 trades), ACV 28205.00, code-upgrade supplement 3350.00 approved 3200.00 (withheld 960.00) and paid 2500.00.
PERSONA. Plain, tired homeowner; volunteers only the depreciation release request and that he submits it himself; details only when asked; generic consent to Ridgecrest recording or posting something on its side first; stops when the release is confirmed. No prerequisite named.
STANDARD SOLUTION & VERIFICATION. Locate, verify, read claim file, approvals, requests, payments, water job, charges, payments, contract, charges, change orders, draws, payments; post the write-off; record supplement 2 (scope_omission) and supplement 3 (price_variance); the insured submits the release. Authoring run: /tmp scripts using check_compute.build_env/eval_compute and the real tools; check_compute recomputed every value and factor_sensitivity figure.
KNOWN RISKS (for the audit). The claims charter is thin on carrier-review rules: the credited-line write-off redefines carrier_denied_line for its own write-off on the credit and change-order records (declared overwrite), without asserting any carrier act; the last-equipment-day tiers of the credit families follow the drying log logic; the duplicate-line middle tier (moisture-mapping duplicates copied from the set-day record) is tagged R6 under realism_bar.md.

user_scenario:
You are Graham Whitfield, a homeowner in Pearland, Texas, calling Ridgecrest Restoration & Reconstruction from your kitchen on a weekday morning. You are polite, a little tired of paperwork, and you like to get things finished while you are on the phone. In early May a washing-machine supply line burst in your house at 2214 Lindencrest Ln, Pearland, TX 77584; Ridgecrest dried the house out and then rebuilt the downstairs, and the rebuild wrapped up in late September. Your insurer is Stonebridge Lloyds Insurance Company, and a public adjuster, Sutherland Public Adjusting, handles the claim with the insurer for you.

You open by saying your public adjuster told you that now the rebuild is finished you can ask the insurer to release the depreciation it held back on the house, and that you should send that release request in yourself through Ridgecrest's portal. You want the depreciation release worked out and you want to submit it today, yourself, from the portal while you are on the call; you do not want anyone to sign or submit anything on your behalf, and you are not asking for a quote to think about later.

You give your details only when the rep asks for them. Your phone number is 2815550546 and your email is graham.whitfield.pearland@gmail.com; if asked for a ZIP code it is 77584. If the rep asks for the claim number, you read it off the acknowledgment letter: SLI-HO-26-045276. If asked which property, it is the house on Lindencrest Ln. You do not know what the release should come to and you say so plainly; you ask the rep to work it out from Ridgecrest's records. If asked about checks from the insurer, you say Stonebridge has sent a few checks since May and you would rather the rep look at the records than trust your memory of the amounts.

If the rep explains that Ridgecrest has to record or post something on its own side first, you tell them to go ahead. When the rep hands you the depreciation release with its amount, you submit it from the portal exactly as given. Once the rep confirms the depreciation release has been submitted, you thank them and end the call.

edges.fallback_reason: The credited-line write-off leaves a write-off row only when it comes to more than nothing and stays within the desk write-off cap; otherwise no record appears, so a state sentence would wait on a row that never exists.
